headline: ANDERSON et al. v. THE STATE.
source: Court of Appeals of Georgia (Georgia Appeals Reports, via the Caselaw Access Project)
blurb: The Georgia Court of Appeals ruled against parents who, citing their religion, refused the shots that the Tattnall County school board required for school attendance, a list that included diphtheria.

headline: Evaluation of Vaccination Strategies in Public Clinics -- Georgia, 1985-1993
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Among children served by Georgia's public health clinics, the share who were up to date on their shots rose from 35% in 1987 to 80% in 1993.

headline: Hepatitis A Vaccination of Men Who Have Sex With Men -- Atlanta, Georgia, 1996-1997
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: From January through September 1996, 222 hepatitis A cases were reported in Atlanta residents, a 730% increase from the yearly average of 27 in 1993 to 1995, and health officials planned a vaccination campaign.

headline: First Confirmed Case of Measles in Georgia
source: Georgia Department of Public Health (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: Georgia's health department confirmed the state's first reported measles case since 2012, in an infant who had arrived in Atlanta from outside the United States.

headline: DPH Identifies Likely Source of Measles in Cobb County, Additional Cases Confirmed
source: Georgia Department of Public Health (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: Georgia health officials said the likely source of a measles outbreak in Cobb County was five cases in one family in early October, and confirmed two more cases.

headline: DPH Confirms Measles Case in Metro Atlanta - MMR Vaccine is Safe and Effective in Preventing Measles
blurb: Georgia's health department confirmed measles in an unvaccinated metro Atlanta resident who caught the virus while traveling within the United States.

headline: DPH Confirms Three New Measles Cases Close Contacts of Previous Case
blurb: Georgia's health department confirmed three new measles cases in close contacts of a person whose case was confirmed on September 11, 2025.
